newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens Nixdorf sees higher 96/97 profits.
newsitem.headline: Siemens Nixdorf sees higher 96/97 profits.

text.p: Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG,(SNI) the computer division of German electronics giant Siemens AG, said on Thursday it expects profits and sales to improve in the new business year.

The company's after-tax profits rose by around six million marks to 29 million marks in the business year that ended on September 30, SNI chief executive Gerhard Schulmeyer said in a speech prepared for delivery at a news conference.
The statement said SNI expected "a further increase in sales, particularly in its business solutions and services".
Speaking to Reuters ahead of the news conference, Schulmeyer added: "We have to learn to grow in double-digits."
SNI 1995/96 pre-tax earnings slipped 16 percent to 52 million marks, disappointing analysts who have been closely following the company's massive restructuring of the past few years.
Analysts said SNI could double profits next year and see sales rise around four percent.
Although it was profitable for the second consecutive year in the 1995/96 business year, the PC, mainframe and minicomputer maker fell short of its target of at least 10 percent sales growth.
The company made profits of 62 million marks in 1994/95 after years of huge losses following the unit's formation after Siemens' 1990 take-over of Nixdorf.
